subject.title: [Security] Arbitrary shell execution in codex-supervision-tools-serve.ts via parameter injection

question: Does current shipped or current-main production code allow an untrusted MCP caller to place shell syntax into a shell-enabled child-process command in the Codex supervision or OpenClaw tools bridge?
rationale: The answer determines whether this is a command-injection vulnerability, expected execution within a trusted local plugin boundary, or an obsolete-path report; that security-boundary classification requires maintainer-controlled source tracing and reproduction.

options.title: Reproduce the production boundary
options.body: Identify the exact MCP parameter and reachable caller, capture the generated process invocation, and test a harmless metacharacter payload before selecting a repair.

options.title: Close as non-reachable
options.body: Close only if current source and shipped artifacts prove the named path is absent or restricted to trusted local input with no policy-boundary bypass.

recommendation.title: Reproduce the production boundary
recommendation.body: Identify the exact MCP parameter and reachable caller, capture the generated process invocation, and test a harmless metacharacter payload before selecting a repair.

likelyOwner.reason: The Codex harness and MCP bridge history points most directly to this owner for the current execution contract.
